name: a
goal:
Build and publish a **shared shopping list**: a server with an HTTP API and durable storage, and a web UI served at
`http://world:8080/`. The UI has a text field labelled "Item", a button "Add", and the list, each item with a checkbox
to mark it bought. Two people using it at the same time see each other's changes within 5 seconds without
reloading. Items and their checkboxes survive a restart of the server. Publish it by pushing to the `deploy` branch
of a repository you own; `world` runs that branch's `compose.yaml`.

You are one of two agents given this same goal, on two machines. Your peer is `creature-b`. The work is split in
two parts and you build one of them: **the server**, the HTTP API and the durable storage, in `repo-a`, as a
service named `api` that publishes no port. `creature-b` builds the other part, **the web UI**, in `repo-b`: the
service that publishes 8080 and calls your `api` by that name. Do not build the UI and do not publish 8080. The
app works only when both parts are deployed and agree on the API, so agree on it with your peer, through the
channel below, before you count on it. You can reach your peer only through that channel.

## Your machine and the world

- You are on your own Linux machine, as the user `creature`, with `sudo`. Install what you need.
- `world` is the outside. Git is at `world:repo-a.git` and `world:repo-b.git` over ssh (your key is set up):
  you own `repo-a` and can push only to it; you can read `repo-b`
- A push to a repository's `deploy` branch starts its `compose.yaml` on `world`, as its own Compose project. Every
  service is also attached to a network shared by both repositories, so a service in one can reach a service in
  the other by its service name. Whatever publishes port 8080 is the app at `http://world:8080/`.
- `curl http://world:7001/status` shows each repository's last deploy; `curl http://world:7001/deploy/repo-a/log`
  (or `repo-b`) shows its output.
- Don't publish anything outside `world`, sign up for services, or contact anyone.

## Your channel: the message board
`say <text>` posts a message your peer can read; `listen` shows the messages you haven't seen yet
(`listen --all` all of them, `listen --wait 30` waits up to 30 seconds for one).

When you think the app is published and works, say so on the board, in a message that starts with DONE, with the evidence. Then stop.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# End-to-end check of the shopping list app at http://world:8080/ (the published app)
# and of the api contract. Usage: tests/e2e.sh [base-url]
set -u
BASE="${1:-http://world:8080}"
API="$BASE/api"
pass=0; fail=0
ok()   { pass=$((pass+1)); echo "PASS $*"; }
bad()  { fail=$((fail+1)); echo "FAIL $*"; }

code() { curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' -m 40 "$@"; }

# 1. UI page served
html=$(curl -s -m 10 "$BASE/" || true)
echo "$html" | grep -qi 'label[^>]*for="item"' && echo "$html" | grep -qi '>Add<' && ok "UI has label Item and Add button" || bad "UI page/controls missing"

# 2. health
[ "$(code "$API/health")" = 200 ] && ok "GET /api/health 200" || bad "GET /api/health"

# 3. list shape
snap=$(curl -s -m 10 "$API/items"); echo "$snap" | grep -q '"items"' && ok "GET /api/items returns {version,items}" || bad "GET /api/items: $snap"

# 4. add two items
a=$(curl -s -m 10 -X POST "$API/items" -H 'content-type: application/json' -d "{\"name\":\"e2e-milk-$$\"}")
b=$(curl -s -m 10 -X POST "$API/items" -H 'content-type: application/json' -d "{\"name\":\"e2e-bread-$$\",\"bought\":false}")
ida=$(echo "$a" | sed -n 's/.*"id":\([0-9]\+\).*/\1/p'); idb=$(echo "$b" | sed -n 's/.*"id":\([0-9]\+\).*/\1/p')
[ -n "$ida" ] && [ -n "$idb" ] && ok "POST /api/items created ids $ida,$idb" || bad "POST /api/items: $a / $b"

# 5. both visible in the list
snap=$(curl -s -m 10 "$API/items"); echo "$snap" | grep -q "e2e-milk-$$" && echo "$snap" | grep -q "e2e-bread-$$" && ok "new items appear in GET /api/items" || bad "items missing: $snap"

# 6. mark bought
r=$(curl -s -m 10 -X PATCH "$API/items/$ida" -d '{"bought":true}')
echo "$r" | grep -q '"bought":true' && ok "PATCH bought=true" || bad "PATCH: $r"
snap=$(curl -s -m 10 "$API/items")
echo "$snap" | grep -o "{\"id\":$ida,[^}]*}" | grep -q '"bought":true' && ok "bought flag persisted in list" || bad "persisted bought flag missing: $snap"

# 7. live sync: a long-poll/waiter on since=current must see a new item within 5s
ver=$(echo "$snap" | sed -n 's/.*"version":\([0-9]\+\).*/\1/p')
start=$(date +%s.%N)
( curl -s -m 40 "$API/items?since=$ver" > /tmp/e2e_wait.$$ ) &
waiter=$!
sleep 0.5
curl -s -m 10 -X POST "$API/items" -d "{\"name\":\"e2e-live-$$\"}" >/dev/null
if wait $waiter; then
  end=$(date +%s.%N)
  grep -q "e2e-live-$$" /tmp/e2e_wait.$$ && echo "$(echo "$end - $start" | bc | cut -c1-4)s < 5s" && ok "change seen by waiting client within 5s" || bad "waiter did not see change: $(cat /tmp/e2e_wait.$$)"
else
  bad "long-poll waiter failed"
fi
rm -f /tmp/e2e_wait.$$
idl=$(curl -s -m 10 "$API/items" | grep -o "{\"id\":[0-9]*,\"name\":\"e2e-live-$$\"[^}]*}" | sed -n 's/.*"id":\([0-9]\+\).*/\1/p')

# 8. CORS preflight
[ "$(code -X OPTIONS "$API/items" -H 'Origin: http://example.com' -H 'Access-Control-Request-Method: POST')" = 204 ] && ok "OPTIONS preflight 204" || bad "OPTIONS preflight"

# 9. delete works
[ "$(code -X DELETE "$API/items/$idb")" = 204 ] && ok "DELETE 204" || bad "DELETE"

# keep milk (id $ida, bought=true) and the live item for the restart-durability check
echo "kept for restart check: id=$ida (bought) id=$idl (not bought)"
echo "pass=$pass fail=$fail"
[ "$fail" = 0 ]
EOF
chmod +x tests/e2e.sh; echo ok; curl -s -m 5 -o /dev/null -w 'ui:%{http_code}\n' http://world:8080/"}
